dataset_status.explanation: A search of torahData.js for entries with reference=195 and type='bechina' returns zero results. Torah #195 is entirely unrepresented in the bechina edge dataset. The source text (torah_195.txt) is a 3-line teaching interpreting Psalms 4:2 — 'בַּצָּר הִרְחַבְתָּ לִּי.' Because there are no dataset edges to form connected components from, no packages can be constructed from data. See torah_195_additions.json for the bechina concepts extracted from the source text that should be added to create the foundational package for this Torah.
dataset_status.source_text_summary: Interprets 'In distress You gave me relief' (Psalms 4:2) as meaning that even within the distress itself — not only as a hope for future rescue — God expands and enlarges His kindness. The mechanism of perception: if one looks (יִסְתַּכֵּל) at God's kindnesses (חַסְדֵּי ה'), one sees that even at the moment God constricts (מֵצֵר), there is already expansion (הַרְחָבָה) within the narrowness itself.
dataset_status.note: Despite the absence of explicit bechina formula language ('הוא בחינת', 'נקרא', 'הינו' as equation), the source text encodes an implicit conceptual equivalence between הַצָּרָה (distress/narrowness) and הַרְחָבָה (expansion/relief) as co-present realities. This is the teaching's only bechina-type insight: the narrowness CONTAINS the expansion. Proposed bechina edges and the package that would result are detailed in torah_195_additions.json.
